explanation: push_back(T&&) and push_front(T&&) move their argument once, push_back(const T&) copies it once. Each element is one heap node; the sentinel is part of the List and is not allocated.

Iterators 0 and 1 point at 20 and 30. insert(it, 15) puts 15 before 20 and returns an iterator to it; it0 still points at 20. Erasing 15 returns an iterator to the next element (20). Postfix ++ returns the old position and moves it0 to 30. emplace builds 25 in place, before 30.

splice relinks nodes: list 0's elements move in front of 8 without being copied or moved, and iterator 1 still points at 2, now in list 1. Splicing one element moves 2 to the front of list 1. reverse relinks every node; iterators keep pointing at the same elements.
An empty list's begin() equals end(); copying, moving, splicing and reversing empty lists work and allocate nothing.
insert puts the new element before pos (at the front for begin(), at the back for end()) and returns an iterator to it; iterators to other elements stay valid.
emplace builds the element in place from its forwarded arguments: no copy, no move.
erase returns an iterator to the element after the erased one (end() after the last); it destroys the element and frees its node, and every other iterator stays valid.
Prefix and postfix ++, prefix --, and == behave as for any bidirectional iterator.
Moving a list relinks its nodes to the new list's sentinel: no element is touched, iterators to elements stay valid and now point into the new list, and the source is left empty and usable.
Move assignment destroys the target's elements, takes over the source's nodes and leaves the source empty. l = std::move(l) leaves l unchanged.
A copy copies each element once, in order, and is independent of the original. Copy assignment destroys the target's old elements.
l = l must leave l unchanged.
splice(pos, other) moves all of other before pos in O(1), updating both sizes; splicing an empty list changes nothing.
Splicing an element of the same list before itself, or before the element right after it, is a no-op; elsewhere it relinks the node. The size does not change.
reverse relinks the nodes in O(n) without touching any element; iterators keep pointing at the same elements.
clear destroys every element and frees every node; the list is then empty and reusable.
The destructor destroys each element exactly once and frees each node.
